output.myth: When a boat did not come home, the women of the cliff set Tessal on the hearth, filled it with sea-water, and waited. Nobody sat by it. You do not sit beside a kettle for a drowned man; you put it on and get on with your mending. When Aun cut the string, the wind carried Tessal down the Leeward side, where the lamps are low, and it hangs there now with its spout turned toward home. Kael casts past it every night and hauls up only steam, and grumbles. Hesk counts it each turn of the Reel and has never once seen it boil. That is the way of it. If it boils, the one out there is climbing the cliff path with wet boots and an empty belly, and someone had better have the tea ready. So keep the kettle full, child, and keep your hands busy.
output.verse:
Set the kettle on
for the one still out past the sky
it will never boil

problems: The blind guess ('hooded, robed figure standing front-on') does not match the kettle. The domed lid and arched bail above a round body read as a hood over a robe, so the silhouette is ambiguous. The guesser's second alternative (a bell or vase with a dome top) is closer to the intended subject.

Key stars sit on the right parts: spout tip (25985) at the left, spout-to-body join (25606), foot (23685) at the bottom right of the body, lid knob (24244) and dome crown (24327) at the top, and the three flame tongues (25045, 24505, 23430) below. The figure is upright.
The silhouette reads as a rounded outline rather than a bold kettle. The bail is a thin arc that merges with the lid outline, and the spout is short and thin.

Labels overlap in several places: 'the knob on top of the lid' collides with 'crown of the lid dome' and 'top of the bail', and 'rim of the body' runs into 'outer curve of the bail'. This is a labelling problem, not a drawing problem, but it hurts legibility.
The gold stick lines are thin and the blue outline is faint, so the silhouette is hard to read as a solid object.
